method: Uses the ASTM D341 Walther equation log10(log10(v + 0.7)) = A - B log10(T), with v the kinematic viscosity in cSt (mm2/s) and T the absolute temperature in kelvin, so T = degrees Celsius + 273.15. The two measured points fix the line: with Y = log10(log10(v + 0.7)), B = (Y_cold - Y_hot) / (log10 T_hot - log10 T_cold) and A = Y_cold + B log10 T_cold. The viscosity at a temperature is 10^(10^(A - B log10 T)) - 0.7 cSt, and the temperature that reaches a target viscosity is 10^((A - Y_target) / B) - 273.15 degrees Celsius. The colder and hotter reference points are identified from the two temperatures, so their order in the form does not matter. Both measured viscosities must be at least 2 cSt: below that ASTM D341 adds a low-viscosity correction this page does not model, so the page refuses those readings. The hotter point must read lower than the colder one. Inputs are limited to 2 to 100,000 cSt and -50 to 300 degrees Celsius, the target temperature must fall inside that range, and the fit must give a positive viscosity at the check temperature. Warnings appear when the answer lies more than 60 degrees outside the measured span, when it exceeds 200 degrees, and when the two reference temperatures are less than 20 degrees apart. Temperatures are rounded to 0.1 degree and viscosities to 0.01 cSt. The fit is a two-point interpolation: it does not model the low-viscosity correction, wax or asphaltene behaviour, the blending of two fuels, or the measurement uncertainty of the laboratory test.
